newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Britain concerned over Iran air strike ability.
newsitem.headline: Britain concerned over Iran air strike ability.

text.p: British Rear Admiral Alan West voiced concern on Wednesday at growing Iranian military power, including an effort to develop an air-to-surface missile capability.
"We think they are working more on air-to-surface missiles," he told reporters aboard a British aircraft carrier that anchored on Wednesday a km (mile) off Kuwait City.
"I can't really get into more details or I'll be stepping into sensitive areas," added the commander of a UK Task Group which is visiting several Gulf Arab states.
But Western military sources told Reuters Iran was believed to be trying to mount Chinese radar-guided C-801 air-launched missiles on its American F-4 Phantom warplanes.
"It is the air-launch version of the C-802," one said.

Washington was alarmed when Iran successfully test-fired the Chinese-made 60-mile-range (96 km) C-802 missile on January 6 from a ship outside the Gulf, restoring a ship-to-ship strike capability lost during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.

Iran is believed to have some 40 Phantoms but about 30 are not serviceable, sources say. Since the 1979 Islamic revolution, Iran has been starved of spare parts for mainly American arms bought under the late pro-Western shah.
Western powers and their allies on the Arab side of the Gulf, through which some 15 million barrels of oil are exported every day, often criticise Iran's rearmament programme.
"As a military man, if you add all this together one wonders why are they building up this capability? Clearly it must be of concern," said Rear Admiral West.
"My concern has to be with what do they exactly have in terms of equipment and there is no doubt in the maritime sense that they are steadily improving," West added.
Western powers are watching for the expected delivery of a third Russian Kilo-class submarine to Iran, the only regional state to deploy such vessels which also operates "mini-subs".

"They have got a lot of learning still to do. But you do not have to be very capable of operating conventional submarines if you have a clever torpedo to be able to cause quite a lot of havoc against civil targets like large tankers," West warned.
